p01.why: An overloaded || is a function call that evaluates both operands, so make runs once and r is true.

p02.why: The right operands are never evaluated, so the call to a function that is not constexpr does not matter.

p03.why: Both temporaries live to the end of the full expression and are destroyed in reverse order, giving 1, 2, -2, -1, 9.

p04.why: !a == b applies ! only to the left side of a comparison, so -Wlogical-not-parentheses warns and -Werror makes it an error.

p05.why: Short-circuiting gives one call for a, one for b, and four for c, so calls is 6 with a false, b true, c true.

p06.why: Each assertion holds by the truth tables.

p07.why: and is the token &&, bitand is &, and compl is ~, so the declarations are int&&, int&, and a destructor.

p08.why: The division by zero is never evaluated for d == 0, and f(2) is true.

p09.why: The overloaded operators evaluate both operands, left first, so the order is a, b, c, d.

p10.why: The overloaded && evaluates make(true) even though the left is false, so side is 1 and r is false.

p11.why: && inside || without parentheses draws -Wparentheses, which -Werror makes an error.

p12.why: && binds tighter than || and ! binds tighter than ==, so each assertion holds; warnings stay warnings.

p13.why: count() runs only for false ||, so calls is 1.

p14.why: The results are bool prvalues, so decltype of the parenthesized expressions is bool.

p15.why: The words are the same operators with the same precedence, and each assertion holds.

p16.why: An array and a function convert to non-null pointers, so both are true; the compilers only warn.

p17.why: The parentheses around !a show the intent, so no warning is given.

p18.why: g() has type void, which is not a valid operand.

p19.why: Volatile bool operands convert normally, and every term is true.

p20.why: S has no conversion to bool.

p21.why: An explicit operator bool works by contextual conversion, and the arithmetic and pointer operands all give the asserted values.

p22.why: Each left operand's increment completes first, so a is true and b is true with i equal to 2.

p23.why: A throw expression has type void, which is not a valid operand of ||.

p24.why: The && is in parentheses, so -Wparentheses does not warn.

p25.why: The right operand is evaluated and calls a function that is not constexpr, so h() is not constant.

p26.why: GCC 16, Clang, and EDG accept nullptr as an operand and compile; GCC 14 rejects it.

p27.why: Both conversions to int and to double can reach bool, so the conversion is ambiguous.

p28.why: Each result is a bool prvalue.

p29.why: Unscoped enumerators and a class with a conversion to int are valid operands, and each assertion holds.

p30.why: count() runs only for true &&, so calls is 1.

p31.why: A scoped enumeration is not a valid operand of !.

p32.why: A null member pointer is false and &S::m is true, so the condition holds.

p33.why: For d = 0 the right operand is evaluated and divides by zero, so fits(0) is not constant.

p34.why: r is true, z is 2 | 5 = 7, and x goes 2, 3, 7.
